facts.value: Religion has had a significant impact on the political system in many countries.
The sharia affects up to 23% of the global population, or 1.57 billion people who are Muslims.
51% of voters in the United States would be less likely to vote for a presidential candidate who did not believe in God.
Christians made up 92% of members of the US Congress, compared with 71% of the general public (in 2014).
23% of US adults are religiously unaffiliated, with only one former member of Congress (Kyrsten Sinema, Arizona) claiming no religious affiliation.
In most European countries, religion has a much smaller influence on politics compared to the past.
Same-sex marriage and abortion were illegal in many European countries until recently, following Christian doctrine.
Several European leaders are atheists, including France's former president Francois Hollande and Greece's prime minister Alexis Tsipras.
India is still one of the most religious countries where religion has a strong impact on politics.
Hindu nationalists have been targeting minorities like Muslims and Christians in India.
Secularization is the transformation of the politics of a society from close identification with a particular religion's values and institutions toward nonreligious values and secular institutions.
The purpose of secularization is frequently modernization or protection of the population's religious diversity.
